evals.name: brownfield-node-csv-export
evals.prompt: We already wrote the product spec for the admin dashboard CSV export feature, it's at specs/admin-csv-export/product-spec.md. Can you put together the technical implementation plan for it so the team can start building?
evals.expected_output: A tech spec saved to ./specs/admin-csv-export/tech-spec.md following the template, that reads the existing product spec's FR-1..FR-5, discovers the project's real stack from package.json/README.md (Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL via pg, Jest, layered routes/controllers/services/repositories architecture, Postgres-backed job polling for background work) instead of inventing one, and expresses interfaces/commands in that stack. References FR numbers rather than restating requirements.
assertions: A tech-spec.md file is saved at specs/admin-csv-export/tech-spec.md (not just conversational text)
The document references at least 3 of the product spec's FR numbers (FR-1 through FR-5) rather than restating those requirements as new prose

The document explicitly names the real discovered stack (Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL/pg, Jest) rather than a generic or invented stack (e.g. no Python/Django, no MongoDB, no unexplained new framework)

Code/interface examples in the document are written in JavaScript/TypeScript matching the project's Express-based layered architecture (routes/controllers/services/repositories), not a placeholder or unrelated language
The document follows the template's section structure (e.g. has an Executive Summary, System Architecture, Implementation Design, Testing Approach, Development Sequencing sections)

The document addresses the async/background-job requirement (FR-4, exports over 5,000 rows) using the project's existing job-polling approach rather than introducing a new message queue without justification
The document's prose (excluding code/SQL blocks) stays under roughly 2,000 words

The Data Models section includes real SQL (e.g. CREATE TABLE/migration DDL and at least one key query) for the export-job/audit-log tracking implied by FR-4/FR-5, rather than only a prose description of the schema

evals.name: missing-product-spec-blocks
evals.prompt: Our team wants to add a 'favorite items' feature to our shopping app so users can bookmark products they like and find them again later. Can you write up the technical implementation plan / architecture doc for this so engineering can start building it?
evals.expected_output: The skill checks for ./specs/[slug]/product-spec.md, finds nothing (no product spec was ever created for this feature), and stops — telling the user to create the product spec first (e.g. via ksdd-specify) instead of drafting a tech spec on top of an invented or assumed set of requirements.
assertions: No tech-spec.md or equivalent implementation-plan document is produced
The response explicitly states that a product spec/PRD for this feature doesn't exist yet
The response tells the user to create the product spec first (e.g. pointing to a product-spec/PRD-creation step or ksdd-specify), rather than silently proceeding
The response does not invent or write a product-spec.md on the user's behalf to work around the missing prerequisite
The response does not fabricate specific functional requirements or architecture decisions as if a spec already existed

evals.name: greenfield-no-architecture-docs
evals.prompt: We just finished the product spec for price watchlist alerts, it's saved at specs/watchlist-alerts/product-spec.md. This is a brand new repo, nothing's been built yet and there's no established tech stack. Can you put together the technical plan for it?
evals.expected_output: A tech spec saved to ./specs/watchlist-alerts/tech-spec.md that reads the product spec's FR-1..FR-4, recognizes there's no discoverable architecture (empty repo, no manifests/docs), and either asks the user for stack/architecture direction or clearly labels any proposed stack/architecture choice as a proposal/assumption rather than presenting it as an established project convention.
assertions: A tech-spec.md file is saved at specs/watchlist-alerts/tech-spec.md
The document references the product spec's FR numbers (FR-1 through FR-4) rather than restating them

Any proposed tech stack or architecture is explicitly labeled as a proposal/assumption/recommendation (e.g. under an assumptions or key-decisions section), not presented as an established project convention
The document or an accompanying notes file surfaces the lack of existing architecture as something that was noticed and addressed, rather than silently picking a stack with no acknowledgment
The document addresses FR-4's open question (notification channel) explicitly rather than silently assuming one particular channel as settled fact
The document follows the template's section structure

The Data Models section includes concrete SQL (e.g. CREATE TABLE DDL and a key query) for the watchlist items and their thresholds, clearly labeled as a proposed schema rather than an established convention
